newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to give N.Korea $15 mln more food aid - sources.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to give N.Korea $15 mln more food aid - sources.

text.p: The United States is expected to provide $15 million in additional food aid to famine-threatened North Korea, administration and congressional sources said on Tuesday.
The formal announcement was expected later at the State Department news briefing.
The new contribution, which responds to a U.N. World Food Programme appeal, would bring total U.S. food aid to the isolated Stalinist regime in Pyongyang to $33.4 million since late 1995.

The WFP has called for $95.5 million for 200,000 tons of food. But North Korea is believed to be nearly out of food stocks and has said its requirements for the year could be as high as two million tons.

The new U.S. donation comes on the eve of a critical meeting at which North Korea is to tell the United States and South Korea whether it will agree to their year-old proposal to launch peace talks aimed at replacing the Korean War armistice with a durable peace treaty.

U.S. officials say such food donations are based on humanitarian assessments. But Pyongyang has said its food shortages are so severe that it could not consider the peace talks until food aid was made available.
"The United States government has decided to provide humanitarian assistance in the amount of 50,000 metric tons of corn," Burns said.
The aid would be provided under the Title II of the PL-480 program, which requires purchase of U.S. commodities in the United States, he said.
He said the aid was agreed after consultation with the governments of South Korea and Japan.
